jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Haunted Office
jokes.joke: I think my office is haunted. Every morning I open a spreadsheet I definitely saved, and somehow the numbers have changed overnight. My coworkers say it’s probably user error. Absolutely not. If I’m going to spend eight hours a day staring at Excel, I need to believe at least one thing in this building has a soul.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Cubicle Séance
jokes.joke: I told my coworker I think our office is haunted. She said, 'Why?' I said, 'Every night I leave my desk spotless, and every morning there's a ghost sitting in my chair, wearing my clothes, answering my emails, sighing at my life choices.' She said, 'Steve, that's you. You just described a job.' I said, 'That's exactly what a ghost would say.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Unpermitted Entry
jokes.joke: I learned the hard way you can't just organically join a parade. Apparently, marching behind the local rotary club with a stray dog and a kazoo is 'disrupting a permitted event.' And let me tell you, the worst part of being arrested at a parade is the atmosphere. You’re getting handcuffed against a barricade, trying to hold onto a shred of dignity, while a four-story inflatable Snoopy just floats there, cheerfully mocking your life choices.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Bad Possession
jokes.joke: The other day I got possessed by a ghost. Not the fun kind that slides chairs around—this one was possessive. It kept checking my phone, asking who I was texting, and when I tried to leave the house it slammed the door and said, 'Where do you think you're going?'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Haunted Productivity
jokes.joke: I work in an office so dull that when a ghost showed up, nobody screamed. My manager just said, "Great, another employee who's willing to stay after hours." A week later the ghost quit too. It left a note saying, "I crossed over to escape eternal suffering, and somehow this is worse."

scores.comment: Clear stage premise and solid rhythm, but the 'office worker is already a ghost' turn is familiar and the final tag adds only a modest extra laugh.
Concrete, visual, and naturally escalating; the inflatable Snoopy image is memorable and the final contrast lands cleanly, though it stops just short of an exceptional punch.
Understandable and economical, but it relies heavily on the possessed/possessive wordplay and mostly extends that single premise rather than delivering a strong final turn.
Well-structured and readable with a clear escalation, but the miserable-office-versus-eternal-suffering comparison is a familiar workplace-comedy route.
Clean and relatable but the turn is mild; punchline restates the premise rather than escalating.
Strong visual contrast (inflatable Snoopy vs. handcuffs), good escalation and specific imagery carry the laugh.
Fun conceit blending possessive ghost with jealous partner; ending lands but could push further.
Nice double-turn with the ghost quitting too; office deadpan tone sustains well to a sharp final line.
Strong punchline blending the banality of Excel with the desire for a soul. Natural stage rhythm and very grounded.
Relies too heavily on an extended 'she said, I said' dialogue structure. The existential depression trope feels familiar.
A neat pun on 'possessed/possessive', but leans entirely on a standard toxic-partner trope without much escalation.
The 'work is worse than hell' punchline is a very common trope. Lacks specific, grounded details that make stand-up work.
Competent office-ghost observation; the soul line is tidy but the payoff stays soft and familiar.
Clean double turn from self-as-ghost to the denial; dialogue rhythm lands a genuine mild laugh.
Specific visual of Snoopy floating over the arrest carries the laugh; strong stage image and concrete details.
Solid escalation from dull workplace to the ghost’s quit note; clean closer with a clear comic snap.
Clean office-paranormal premise with a solid final line; familiar angle but well executed.
Nice escalation and callback; job-as-ghost metaphor lands, though the twist is fairly predictable.
Strong visual image with the inflatable Snoopy ending; clear premise, escalation, and punchy final picture.
Simple possessive-ghost characterization; understandable and concise, but the turn is straightforward and mild.
